user.title: Microsoft Family Safety
user.description: Configure the integration. After Submit, Home Assistant opens the Microsoft sign-in through a temporary authentication proxy. Sign in with the parent account and answer **Yes** to "Stay signed in?": that is what keeps the Family session valid for about a year instead of a few hours. If Home Assistant is not reachable over HTTPS, local HTTP can be explicitly enabled for testing; Microsoft credentials are then not transport-encrypted on the local network.

data.allow_insecure_http_auth: Allow insecure local HTTP authentication (testing only)

data_description.platforms: Windows, Xbox, Mobile: one lock switch per ticked platform. Ticking Xbox also turns on Xbox play time and the Xbox lock, which need the Microsoft web session (some accounts must renew it with a sign-in every 24 hours). Xbox daily limits work either way. Leave Xbox unticked if you do not need the Xbox lock or Xbox play time: the integration then runs on the mobile token only, with a shorter sign-in.

check_mobile_proxy.title: Microsoft sign-in
check_mobile_proxy.description: Sign in with the Microsoft account that manages the family, and answer **Yes** when Microsoft asks "Stay signed in?". Keep the opened authentication window open: after the visible sign-in completes, Home Assistant switches to a waiting screen while the Family session and the mobile token are established.

check_proxy.title: Microsoft Family web session
check_proxy.description:
**Sign in in the window that just opened**, with the Microsoft account that manages the family, and answer **Yes** to "Stay signed in?".

Then come back here and **wait**: this dialog continues on its own, which can take up to about a minute after the sign-in. Do not press *Open website* again unless the Microsoft window never opened or was closed before you signed in.

data_description.platforms: Windows, Xbox, Mobile: one lock switch per ticked platform. Ticking Xbox also turns on Xbox play time and the Xbox lock, which need the Microsoft web session (some accounts must renew it with a sign-in every 24 hours). Xbox daily limits work either way. Leave Xbox unticked if you do not need the Xbox lock or Xbox play time: the integration then runs on the mobile token only, with a shorter sign-in.
data_description.allowed_users: Leave empty to let every user use the buttons and settings (default). As soon as users are ticked, only they and the administrators can: a child's non-administrator account is refused on every button, switch, limit and time window, and on the microsoft_family_safety actions. Automations and scripts run by Home Assistant are not affected. Give the child a non-administrator account: an administrator can change this option.
data_description.strict_mode: Off by default. When on, a Windows or Xbox lock placed by microsoft_family_safety.lock_platform that Microsoft reports as cancelled (for example from the Family Safety app) while it should still hold is placed again on the next update, at most every 10 minutes, and the event microsoft_family_safety_lock_reasserted is fired. unlock_platform ends it. Keep strict mode off when another integration (Hearth, for example) manages these locks: strict mode would place a lock again after a parent released it in the Family Safety app, fighting the parent's decision.
data_description.app_usage_sensors: 0 (default) = off. Otherwise each child's most used apps today, up to this number, get a sensor with their minutes used today, and the event microsoft_family_safety_app_usage fires when an app's usage grows between two updates. An app keeps its sensor once it has one.
data_description.xbox_link: Xbox limits, the Xbox lock and Xbox play time then come from the Xbox Family Settings app's service, on their own sign-in, without the web session. Only with Xbox ticked. Usually linked automatically after a sign-in; tick this if the Connection sensor shows xbox_family: not_linked.

lock_platform.name: Lock Platform
lock_platform.description: Lock a platform (Windows/Xbox/Mobile) for a child account until a time. The first lock saves the override Microsoft had in force (a parent's own lock, or none) so unlock_platform can put it back; a lock already in force that ends later is kept. Answers with the saved prior state and the lock applied. Keep strict mode off when another integration (Hearth, for example) manages these locks: strict mode would place a lock again after a parent released it in the Family Safety app, fighting the parent's decision.

Keep strict mode off when another integration (Hearth, for example) manages these locks: strict mode would place a lock again after a parent released it in the Family Safety app, fighting the parent's decision.

sync_site_list.name: Sync Site List
sync_site_list.description: Keep the child's blocked websites in step with a published list of domains (one per line, '#' comments). Adds what the list gained and removes only what this same list added before and has since dropped; sites blocked by hand and allowed sites are left alone, and a domain sharing a site with an allowed one is skipped. The list must be served over https (redirects are not followed), is read up to 1 MiB, and only plain domains are taken. An empty or failed download, or one that would remove most of what the list added, changes nothing; stop removes everything the list added. Answers with what was added, removed, kept and skipped. Administrators only.

xbox_lock_needs_xbox_features.title: The Xbox lock needs the Xbox features
xbox_lock_needs_xbox_features.description:
Something asked {title} to lock or unlock an Xbox, but this entry runs on the mobile token only, and the Xbox lock goes through the Microsoft Family web session.

To turn the Xbox features on, open Settings > Devices & services > Microsoft Family Safety > Configure, tick **Xbox** under Monitored platforms and submit. Home Assistant then asks you to sign in to Microsoft again; answer **Yes** to "Stay signed in?". Some accounts must repeat that sign-in every 24 hours.

If you do not need the Xbox lock, remove the call that asked for it and ignore this issue.
